digest.component_or_area: tickets repository maintenance and reclaim window execution
propositions: A one-time atomic force-with-lease rewrite of the tickets branch reduces repository size from 1.04 GiB to ~94 MiB by deleting pre-rewrite commit history, with correctness verified before publication via pre-push assertions in a scratch clone and post-publication via ancestry and pack-growth checks.

Quiescence enforcement requires GitHub workflow disable, zero in-flight review-bot sessions, completed descendant reconcile-bridge.yml run, stopped rebar-mcp servers, and operator confirmation before any rewrite or force-push can occur.

The epoch-mismatch refusal guard replaces elapsed-time proxy by requiring direct runtime proof: exact host binary and deployed review-bot runtime must both successfully refuse epoch-blind writes before and after the rewrite.
Non-resurrection is proven by asserting old-tip ancestry is false after the first post-window write and verifying no fetched ref descends from the old commit, not by elapsed time or drain completion.

The identity.enforce_since re-pin lands through Gerrit with normal LLM-Review and Verified votes after rewrite publication, with no CI deadlock because require_authenticated=false skips SHA validation.

Post-enable reconciliation is validated by successful reconcile-bridge.yml and canary runs, operator-approved signed CLI sequence with zero mutation/recovery failures and drift_total=0, and final fsck with zero repairable diagnostics.
